calls.head: Pettersson (#40) gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Islanders keep sending Holmström’s line (Pageau, Duclair and Holmström) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter DeBoer has been using this group as a checking line on opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Canucks’ second line is DeBrusk, Pettersson (#40) and Lekkerimäki.

calls.head: Active D against forward-led
calls.body: The Islanders’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Canucks’ not so much. The Islanders are the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Vancouver is near the bottom. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Islanders’ defensemen jump into the play.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Islanders squeak past the Canucks
paras: Matthew Kessel made his Islanders debut, after four seasons with the Blues, and picked up an assist. Kyle Palmieri opened the scoring for the Islanders late in the first. Matias Maccelli scored his first goal for the Islanders 53 seconds later to make it 2-0. Max Sasson got the Canucks on the board midway through the second. Brock Boeser tied it on the power play late in the second. Palmieri struck again early in the third to put the Isles ahead for good.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Ilya Sorokin made 24 saves for the Islanders, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 35 of 38. The Islanders improved to 3-3-0, and the Canucks fell to 2-6-0.

items.text: The Canucks are on a five-game losing streak.
Brayden Schenn got the better of his brother Luke.
Filip Hronek extended his point streak against the Islanders to seven games.
Kyle Palmieri scored his first two goals of the season, his first since Nov 18, 2025 (ten games played since).
